_note: Public holidays for the months the report covers. Used only to judge whether a movement looks seasonal — the wording rules require hedged language, never a stated cause. CN = mainland China (matters because cross-border freight stops), NZ = New Zealand (affects walk-in trade).

2026-01.name: New Year
2026-01.impact: Domestic couriers pause briefly; cross-border largely unaffected

2026-01.name: New Year's Day and day after
2026-01.impact: Walk-in trade quiet over the holiday period

2026-02.name: Waitangi Day
2026-02.impact: Long weekend; some effect on walk-in trade

2026-02.name: Chinese New Year (9-day holiday, New Year's Day 17 Feb)
2026-02.impact: Cross-border collection, customs clearance and freight are suspended or delayed for roughly two weeks either side. This is the most common reason February export volume falls away.

2026-04.name: Easter
2026-04.impact: Four-day weekend; a traditional retail peak in New Zealand

2026-05.name: Labour Day
2026-05.impact: 5-day holiday; freight pause, and a domestic shopping peak in China

2026-07.name: Matariki
2026-07.impact: Public holiday; winter is the quiet season

2026-09.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
2026-09.impact: Gifting peak for honey and supplements in the weeks before

2026-10.name: National Day
2026-10.impact: 7-day holiday; extended freight pause and a domestic shopping peak

2026-12.name: Christmas and Boxing Day (observed 28 Dec)
2026-12.impact: Peak retail season in New Zealand
